---
title: "Automated meta-research"
subtitle: "Designing, running and reviewing meta-research studies with language models, in the open"
toc: true
---

Meta-research is the study of research itself: how transparently it is reported, whether its
data can be found and reused, whether its results survive replication, what happens to it when
it is retracted. This project asks whether that work can be done end to end by language models,
under conditions strict enough that the result is worth reading.

Nothing is hidden. The search that found the literature, the map derived from it, the studies
proposed against that map, the code that runs them, the reviews written by independent models,
and the disagreements between those reviews are all published here, in the order they happened.

## Where this currently stands

The literature has been harvested and described, and four studies have been proposed against
the map. Nothing has been run or reviewed.

| stage | state |
|---|---|
| Search the literature | done, tier A only. [1830 records](corpus.qmd) |
| Map what the field studies | done. [The landscape](landscape.qmd) |
| Propose studies against the gaps | done. [Four protocols](agenda.qmd), three runnable |
| Independent review by two models | waiting. One reviewer is quota-blocked until 2026-09-20 |
| Run them in R | not started |
| Publish results with the reviews | not started |

The review row sits above the run row on purpose. A protocol is published and reviewed before
the analysis is run, not after, so that the reviewers see a design rather than a finding.

## The pipeline

**1. Search.** PubMed and PMC, through a harvester that logs every query it issues and cannot
truncate a result set without saying so. The protocol, including the queries that turned out to
be wrong and why, is in [how this was done](methods.qmd).

**2. Map.** Every record is labelled by vocabulary match against a topic list, and the counts
are derived by a script rather than read by a model. This is deliberately the dumbest possible
method: a claim on [the landscape](landscape.qmd) can be checked by rerunning one file.

**3. Propose.** Studies are proposed against the map, and a proposal has to say what is already
known, which records establish it, and what specifically would be new. A proposal that cannot
name the work it would extend does not get written up.

**4. Run.** Analyses are written and executed in R. Each study carries its data, its code and
its output in the repository, so a reader can rerun it rather than trust it.

**5. Review.** Each study is reviewed independently by models from different providers, given
the study and instructed to refute it. Reviews are published whole, including the ones that
find nothing and the ones that disagree with each other. Where reviewers disagree, the
disagreement is shown rather than resolved silently.

## What the models did and did not do

The searching, the analysis code, the drafting and the reviewing are done by language models.
The research questions, the scope decisions, the judgment about what is worth publishing, and
the responsibility for everything on this site are the author's. Where a model produced
something, the page says which model and when.

This distinction matters more here than in most projects, because the subject is research
quality. A site about transparency that was vague about its own provenance would be evidence
against its own argument.

## Source

Everything, including the harvested corpus and the search log, is at
[github.com/choxos/autometaresearch](https://github.com/choxos/autometaresearch).
